parsed.explanation: The quoted 'infinite sunflower fact' is false as stated: X_i={1,...,i} (or the antichain variant) admits no infinite subfamily with constant pairwise intersection, and the offered induction ('delete that element and continue') never terminates without a size bound. Consequently Lemma 1's general claim is also false — matching the ledger's counterexample F_k={x_1..x_k,y_k}, a pairwise-intersecting family with infinitely many minimal finite transversals. The write-up derives the only clause it needs (finitely many C with |C| <= K) from that false general statement rather than proving the bounded case, and the finiteness of C (hence L6.2) is established nowhere else. Restricting the sunflower fact and Lemma 1 to sets of size <= K repairs it in a sentence.
